question_type: mean of six year-end values from one annual series; vintage (latest revision vs single issue) and dollar-only vs all-currency table decide
decisive_step: Two selections. (1) Table: CM-I-2 'Total Liabilities by Type, Payable in Dollars, Part A.--Foreign Countries', column (1) 'Total foreign countries' (treasury_bulletin_1997_03.txt:3221-3228; Section I 'Liabilities to Foreigners Reported by Banks in the United States', :3186), rather than the CM-I-1/CM-I-3/CM-I-4 foreign-countries totals that include foreign-currency liabilities (~9% higher; v8_prompt's error, error_bin 5-25pct) or IFS-2 (not bank-only). (2) Vintage: take each year's latest printing (1993, 1994, 1995 and 1996 were revised in later issues; printings SUMMARY at a[27], c[10]) rather than the March 1997 issue, the only issue that lists all six years together. The reference chose the single-issue reading (worklog Step 3, solution key_decisions 2) and was graded wrong, while listing the latest-revision mean as its alternative (review.md check 3); v8_none made the same single-issue choice (error_bin within_1pct). All three pilot cells took the latest revisions and were right.

a.path_summary: find_tables on the question nouns (a[5]) ranked CM-I-2 first; show_table of the March 1997 copy (a[8]) showed column (1) 'Total foreign countries' and the year rows. Worried by 'reported by U.S. banks', it detoured to IFS-2, whose column literally says 'Liabilities reported by banks in United States' (a[10]-[12]), and searched for titles/sections with that phrase (a[15], a[17], a[25]) before settling on CM-I-2 because it sits in Section I (a[26]). It ran printings for each of the six years (a[21], re-run for two truncated years at a[27]), took the latest printing of each, and computed the mean with calc (a[29]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: ran printings per year and took the latest printed value of each
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: the reference instead took all six values from the March 1997 issue (worklog Step 5) and was graded wrong; a's latest-revision choice is the graded-right reading

tool_use.friction: a[5] find_tables without --years: 403 parts, OUTPUT CUT at 8000 bytes; a[8] show_table --long --grep 199 paged after 5 of 17 rows; a[19] `sed -n ... treasury_bulletin_1997_03.txt` with a relative path failed silently (`|| true`); a[21] six printings in one shell loop overflowed the page (10754 chars omitted) so two years had to be re-run with tail (a[27]); a[21]/a[27] SUMMARY prints values in %g form (six significant digits, scientific notation), so the model had to read exact 7-digit values from the listing lines; a[23] the officeqa.py search helper returned a dict and iterating it printed only key names ('query', 'query_tokens', 'match_mode', 'results') - unusable.

a.text_use: a[18] 'Need use printings for each year latest' (latest-printing rule); a[29] 'Compute every final number with calc'; a[14] 'narrowing to the one whose columns explicitly say reported by banks' (prefer the table whose headers match the wording) - this sentence drove the IFS-2 detour a[10]-[17] before it returned to CM-I-2

b.path_summary: Two find_tables calls (b[6] overflowed at 1055 parts; b[8] with --years found CM-I-4 and CM-I-2). One show_table --stitch --raw command (b[11]) printed the full March 1997 and March 1998 CM-I-2 tables side by side; b took 1991 from the 1997 copy (the only issue listing it) and 1992-1996 from the later 1998 copy, i.e. the latest revisions, without running printings and without any advice text (b[12]). It checked CM-I-4 (b[14], b[16]) and rejected it as a quarterly by-country table, looked at the raw title lines (b[18], b[20]), computed the mean with calc (b[22]) and submitted once; recorded with no findings (b[25]).

first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: same graded-right reading as a and c; the reference took the single-issue reading

tool_use.friction: b[6] find_tables --rows --all without --years: 1055 parts in 90 groups, OUTPUT CUT; b[16] two --raw pages of the 94-row CM-I-4 (13560 chars omitted) spent on a table it then rejected; b[18] relative-path sed failed silently. Note b never ran printings: its vintage choice rested on the two issues it happened to open, and the 1998_03 copy does carry the final values, but it did not verify that no later issue revised them.

b.harness_use: one submit at call 10, no findings (the later_printing rule did not fire because all six values were already latest), recorded. No loop notes, no compaction.

c.path_summary: find_tables with default listing (c[4]) showed CM-I-2 first with its three newest issues; show_table of the 2001_03 copy (c[6]) confirmed column (1) and CY row keys but that copy starts at 1995. One command with six printings calls (--row CY1991..CY1996, --years 1992-2001) (c[8]) listed every printing; the output was cut in the middle so 1993 was re-run with tail (c[10]). It took the latest printing of each year and computed the mean with calc (c[12]). 14 steps, 25 s: the most efficient cell.

smallest_change.change: No change needed: all three cells chose CM-I-2 column (1) and the latest printing of each year, which is the graded-right reading; the advice text's latest-printing rule is exactly the convention that separates them from the reference and from v8_none (both single-issue). Keep that rule verbatim in v10.

alternatives.change: printings: (a) print exact integers in the SUMMARY value lines instead of %g (otables.py printings_page uses '%g' % val), so the model sees `      <exact 7-digit integer>: 1997_03..1999_06 (8)` rather than `      <d.ddddde+06>: ...` (a[21], a[27], c[8], c[10]); (b) accept several periods in one call (`--row 1991 1992 ... 1996` or `--rows CY1991-CY1996`) and print one compact SUMMARY block per period, so a six-year series does not overflow the 8000-byte page and force re-runs (a[21]->a[27], c[8]->c[10]). The model would have seen six lines like `  [CY1993] col (1): 14 printings, 4 distinct values - REVISED; latest <exact value> in 1999_03 (...:3205)`.
alternatives.why_not_first: Both cells recovered by re-running with tail; the values were read correctly from the listing lines. Efficiency and a hazard (%g rounds 7-digit values on display) rather than a cause of error here.

alternatives.change: find_tables: when the query returns more than ~10 groups without --years, print the top group in full and the rest as one line each with a hint, instead of cutting at 8000 bytes (a[5], b[6]).
alternatives.why_not_first: CM-I-2 was already the first group in every cell's listing, so the cut did not hide the answer.

alternatives.change: Refine 'prefer the table whose title and column headers match the question's wording' with: 'A phrase like "reported by banks" may name the section a table sits in, not a column; check the section banner (rg -n "SECTION" <file>) before switching to a table whose column merely contains the phrase.'
alternatives.why_not_first: It cost a about 8 steps (a[10]-[17], a[25]) but not the answer; b and c never detoured.

fix.irreducible: Partly: the question does not pin an issue, and a strong model (the reference) read it as 'the one issue that lists 1991-1996 together' and was graded wrong, while the latest-revision reading is graded right. Correctness here depends on the corpus-wide convention 'latest printing unless a date is pinned'; with the opposite convention all three cells would be wrong. Not a defect of the adapter, but a reminder that this convention should stay explicit in v10 text or be enforced by the later_printing control.

notes: (1) This question is the clearest evidence in the set that the latest-printing rule earns its place: the reference (single-issue March 1997 vintage) and v8_none (same vintage, within_1pct) are graded wrong, all three pilot cells (latest revisions) are right, and v8_cards was right too. b's mechanism-only arm got there with no text and no printings call because one show_table command (b[11]) put the 1997_03 and 1998_03 copies of the table on the same page; a v10 tool could make that comparison routine (e.g. printings --rows over a year range, or show_table --compare <issue>). (2) The other hazard on this question is the table: v8_prompt took the all-currency foreign-countries total (CM-I-3/CM-I-4 style, ~9% high). The question's '(all types combined)' mirrors the 'by Type' table's total column, and find_tables ranked CM-I-2 first for every cell, so the ranking did the work. (3) printings displays 7-digit values as %g in the SUMMARY (scientific notation with six significant digits, e.g. 'd.ddddde+06'); the listing lines carry exact integers. A model that reads only the SUMMARY would mis-transcribe. (4) Six printings calls in one shell command overflow the page (a[21], c[8]); both cells recovered with `| tail`. (5) show_table --stitch --raw fit two full 17-row tables in one page (b[11]) while --long --grep 199 paged at 5 rows (a[8]): for short wide tables --raw is the efficient view. (6) The officeqa.py search helper is a trap: a[23] iterated its return value and got dict keys; the v10 README could either document `docs.search(...)['results']` or drop the helper now that find_tables exists. (7) find_tables splits CM-I-2 into two groups by title variant ('... Payable in Dollars' vs '... Part A.--Foreign Countries', a[19]); printings by id crosses both, which is what a and c relied on.
